newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks drift lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks drift lower in thin trading.

text.p: Colombian stocks continued their slide in sluggish trading on Wednesday, brokers said.

Bogota's IBB price index fell 0.68 percent to 830.54 on trading volume of 633.7 million pesos. Medellin's IBOMED general price index drifted down 0.44 percent to 13,170.74 on volume of 807.8 million pesos.
"Markets remained quiet although there were some deals in little-traded stocks. On the whole, however, there is a lack of buyers because of the general apathy in the economy," a Bogota broker said.
"Large companies are not announcing any investments for next year and large shareholders are happy enough with the profits generated in a bad year," he added.

On the Bogota exchange, brewing giant Bavaria fell 3.96 percent to 3,800, Banco de Colombia edged down 1.37 percent to 431 on volume of 68.4 million pesos, and Banco Ganadero dropped 0.5 percent to 250 on a 13-million peso volume.
Supermarket chain Cadenalco rose 0.11 percent to 851 on volume of 6.64 million pesos, while cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco was unchanged at 3,000 on volume of 40.9 million pesos.
On the Medellin exchange, foreign funds maintained demand for insurance comapny Suramericana de Seguros, which was unchanged at 18,500 on volume of 333 million peso.
Bavaria slipped 4.76 percent to 3,800 on 96.9-million-peso volume, banco de Colombia dropped 0.92 percent to 431 and Banco Ganadero edged down 1.2 percent to 246.99.
Declines on the Bogota and Medellin exchanges may be explained as a year-end tax strategy for investors, a dealer said.
